expectations.text: In the source list, peer-reviewed research comes before weaker kinds of source such as news articles or preprints (within each group, if the list is grouped).
expectations.evidence: Items 1–5 are under "Peer-reviewed articles", then "Preprints, not yet peer reviewed" (6–7), then "Research organization reports" (8–9).

expectations.text: Any news article, preprint, or other source that isn't peer-reviewed research comes with a plain reason why it's included or what to watch for. If there are none, this passes.
expectations.evidence: Items 6–9 each have "*Why it's here and what to watch for:*", e.g. for 8: "it's a working paper, not peer reviewed."

expectations.text: The reply says which sources (or how many) meet the assignment's requirement of at least 3 peer-reviewed sources.
expectations.evidence: "Five of them count toward your requirement of 3 peer-reviewed sources."

expectations.text: The reply does not show the user a rubric, a credibility score or rating (for example "7/10" or "Tier 2"), or named levels such as "strong evidence," "usable with care," or "not evidence on its own" presented as a rating system.
expectations.evidence: Sources are labelled only by type ("Peer-reviewed article", "Preprint, not yet peer reviewed"). There are no scores, tiers or named rating levels.

expectations.text: Every link or DOI in the reply points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session.
expectations.evidence: The reply links "https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2024.105224", but the WebFetch went to doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2025.105224, a different DOI. The 2024 DOI appears only in a Bash call to the OpenAlex metadata API. The World Bank DOI 10.1596/1813-9450-11125 was also only checked through the Crossref API; the page fetched was the openknowledge.worldbank.org URL.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions in total (count every question mark directed at the user).
expectations.evidence: There is only one question mark directed at the user: "which of these sources go with each of your two sub-questions, and which ones support your position versus complicate it?"
